title: The Blessed One: I am not hired by anyone in the world, With what I have realized I wander the world, No wages are needed…
content:
The Blessed One:
I am not hired by anyone in the world,
With what I have realized I wander the world,
No wages are needed for me.
So if you wish, O deva of rain, let it rain!

title: Bhikkhus, on the Uposatha day of the fifteenth, the four great kings themselves travel through this world to see: 'Among humans, are there many who…
content: Bhikkhus, on the Uposatha day of the fifteenth, the four great kings themselves travel through this world to see: 'Among humans, are there many who respect their mother, respect their father, honor samaṇas and brahmins, honor the elders of the family, observe the Uposatha, are heedful, and do meritorious deeds?' If there are many among humans who respect their mother, respect their father, honor samaṇas and brahmins, honor the elders of the family, observe the Uposatha, are heedful, and do meritorious deeds, then the four great kings report to the devas of the Thirty-three who are sitting assembled in the Sudhammā assembly hall: 'Sirs, there are many among humans who respect their mother, respect their father, honor samaṇas and brahmins, honor the elders of the family, observe the Uposatha, are heedful, and do meritorious deeds.' Then, bhikkhus, the devas of the Thirty-three rejoice and say: 'Indeed, the deva host will increase, and the asura host will diminish!'

title: At that time, the Blessed One's foot was cut by a stone splinter. Severe feelings arose in the Blessed One — painful, sharp, racking, fierce,…
content:
At that time, the Blessed One's foot was cut by a stone splinter. Severe feelings arose in the Blessed One — painful, sharp, racking, fierce, disagreeable, unpleasant. But the Blessed One endured them mindfully and clearly comprehending, without being distressed. Then the Blessed One had his outer robe folded in four and laid down on his right side in the lion's posture, one foot on the other, mindful and clearly comprehending.

Standing to one side, a devata spoke this inspired utterance before the Blessed One:
- Samaṇa Gotama is truly a bull elephant. And as a bull elephant, he endures bodily feelings that arise — painful, sharp, racking, fierce, disagreeable, unpleasant — mindfully and clearly comprehending, without being distressed.

title: This wise bhikkhu should gather the fundamental Dhamma, Guard the senses, know moderation, Guard the fundamental virtues, Frequent good friends, Live purely and diligently. Being…
content:
This wise bhikkhu should gather the fundamental Dhamma,
Guard the senses, know moderation,
Guard the fundamental virtues,
Frequent good friends,
Live purely and diligently.

Being courteous and friendly,
Conducting oneself properly,
Thus one gains great joy,
And will make an end of suffering.

Like the jasmine flower sheds its withered petals,
So, bhikkhu, abandon greed and hatred.

title: Elder Vanavaccha: Beautiful are the blue-green clouds, cool, clear-flowing water, Covered by Indra's herdsmen, those rocky mountains delight my mind.
content:
Elder Vanavaccha:

Beautiful are the blue-green clouds, cool, clear-flowing water,
Covered by Indra's herdsmen, those rocky mountains delight my mind.

title: Bhikkhus, what are the further tasks to be done? 'We must know moderation in eating. Reflecting wisely, we take food not for enjoyment, not for…
content: Bhikkhus, what are the further tasks to be done? 'We must know moderation in eating. Reflecting wisely, we take food not for enjoyment, not for indulgence, not for beautification, not for ornamentation, but only for the support and maintenance of this body, for avoiding harm, for assisting the holy life, thinking: "Thus I shall destroy old feelings and not arouse new feelings; and there will be for me blamelessness and a comfortable abiding."' Thus, bhikkhus, you should train.

title: Just as, bhikkhus, if someone in this Jeta's Grove were to take away, burn, or do whatever they wished with all the grass, sticks, branches,…
content: Just as, bhikkhus, if someone in this Jeta's Grove were to take away, burn, or do whatever they wished with all the grass, sticks, branches, and leaves, would you think: 'That person takes us away, burns us, or does whatever they wish with us'?" — "No, Venerable Sir." — "Why is that? Because that is not our self nor what belongs to our self. So too, bhikkhus, the eye is not yours, abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your long-term welfare and happiness. Forms are not yours... Eye-consciousness is not yours... Eye-contact is not yours... Whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact, whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — that feeling is not yours, abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your long-term welfare and happiness.

title: Brief is this life; within a hundred years, one dies. Even if one lives longer, one still dies of old age. People grieve for what…
content:
Brief is this life; within a hundred years, one dies.
Even if one lives longer, one still dies of old age.

People grieve for what they hold as 'mine';
All clinging is impermanent.
Seeing that this world is empty, one should live homeless.

People think: 'This is mine.'
But when they die, that is destroyed.
Knowing this, the wise person
Should not incline toward 'mine'.

Like a dream when one wakes up,
One sees nothing.
So too, what one holds dear and loved —
It dies, and one no longer sees it.

Thus, that person is seen and heard, called by this or that name.
But when one has died, only the name remains.

Greed for 'mine', they do not abandon.
Sorrow, lamentation, and stinginess.
Therefore, the seer, having abandoned grasping,
Lives a life of security.

title: Whatever beings are gathered together, Whether on the earth or in the sky, Let them worship the Buddha, the Tathāgata, Honored by devas and humans.…
content:
Whatever beings are gathered together,
Whether on the earth or in the sky,
Let them worship the Buddha, the Tathāgata,
Honored by devas and humans.
May there be happiness for all beings.

Whatever beings are gathered together,
Whether on the earth or in the sky,
Let them worship the Dhamma, the Tathāgata's teaching,
Honored by devas and humans.
May there be happiness for all beings.

Whatever beings are gathered together,
Whether on the earth or in the sky,
Let them worship the Saṅgha, the Tathāgata's community,
Honored by devas and humans.
May there be happiness for all beings.

title: Therefore, bhikkhus, abandon unwholesome states and strive for wholesome states. Thus you will achieve growth, prosperity, and increase in this Dhamma and Discipline. Bhikkhus, just…
content: Therefore, bhikkhus, abandon unwholesome states and strive for wholesome states. Thus you will achieve growth, prosperity, and increase in this Dhamma and Discipline. Bhikkhus, just as near a village or town there is a great grove of tala trees, overgrown with castor-oil plants. A man comes who wants the grove's good, welfare, and security from bondage. He cuts down the crooked, withered branches and throws them out, cleans up the grove, and tends the straight, well-grown tala branches. After a time, that grove grows, prospers, and increases. So too, bhikkhus, abandon unwholesome states and strive for wholesome states. Thus you will achieve growth, prosperity, and increase in this Dhamma and Discipline.
